As high pressure shifts offshore through the day, southwesterly
flow will ramp up into the afternoon. Temperatures will warm
into the mid 80s for most areas (even some upper 80s in spots),
on the order of 5 degrees warmer than Saturday. Dewpoints will
also surge back well into the 60s to around 70 degrees by the
afternoon hours, making for a noticeable return in summer-like
humidity. Skies will turn mostly cloudy by the afternoon,
especially along and NW of I-95, which should help negate the
degree of unpleasant humidity.

The main forecast challenge for today will be the potential for
scattered showers and thunderstorms developing later this
afternoon and into tonight. The latest trend in the CAMs has
been for an even later convective initiation time than
before, which will significantly limit any potential for severe
and flash flood threats. The greatest limiting factor appears 
to be a lack of substantial instability until close to sunset, 
with even the highest modeled CAPE largely less than 1,000 
J/kg. This combined with poor lapse rates and weak forcing 
during the peak diurnal time frame should limit coverage for 
much of the daytime hours. However, better forcing does look to 
arrive during the evening to even overnight hours. So at least
some scattered showers and potential for a few thunderstorms are
still anticipated to develop at some point. We still cannot 
totally rule out a couple stronger storms, with gusty winds, 
small hail, and brief heavy downpours possible.

forcing remains aloft.
